entries.description: Code review of Document layer (BaseColor, Document, PageSize, Rectangle) via Gemini Pro with Sonnet cross-verification. Findings: Document.Close() resource leak when writer set but Open() never called; Rectangle lacks value equality; BaseColor naming convention (Red_, Green_, Blue_); EnsureOpen dead code path.

Fixed Document.Close() state consistency: _closed now always set to true. Reordered EnsureOpen() checks so _closed is checked before !_open (dead code fix). Declined Rectangle→record (too invasive for V&V), BaseColor naming (deliberate), thread safety (not applicable).

Test gap analysis and new tests added. RectangleTests: +4 (FourArgConstructor, CopyConstructor independence, ToString, ZeroDimensions). PageSizeTests: +5 (A3, A5, Tabloid, Executive, AllOriginAtZero). DocumentIntegrationTests: +4 (PageNumber tracking, Close-without-Open, Close idempotent, NewPage-after-Close). BaseColorTests: +5 (GetHashCode consistency, null equality, both-null equality, ToString, LightGray/DarkGray).
dotnet build succeeded with 0 warnings, 0 errors. dotnet test: Passed 222, Failed 0.
Cross-provider verification with gemini-pro (1 round). Session review saved to session-reviews/session-001.md.

Code review of PDF primitives (PdfObject, PdfArray, PdfDictionary, PdfBoolean, PdfNull, PdfNumber, PdfName, PdfString, PdfLiteral) via Gemini Pro with Sonnet cross-verification. Critical findings: PdfNumber.FormatDouble can produce scientific notation (forbidden in PDF spec); PdfName.Type hides PdfObject.Type with 'new' keyword. Major findings: PdfString.OriginalBytes exposes internal array; PdfArray allows null elements; PdfString.WriteHex allocates per-byte; PdfNumber(string) stores raw content without normalization; PdfName.EncodeName corrupts non-ASCII chars. Minor: PdfNull redundant WriteTo; PdfBoolean/PdfNull constructors should be private.

Fixed 8 issues: (1) PdfNumber.FormatDouble uses fixed-point '0.######' instead of 'G' to avoid scientific notation (Critical); (2) PdfNumber(string) normalizes stored Bytes via FormatDouble; (3) PdfString.OriginalBytes returns clone to prevent mutation; (4) PdfArray Add/Insert/indexer reject null with ArgumentNullException; (5) PdfString.WriteHex uses byte lookup table instead of per-byte string allocation; (6) PdfNull: reuse NullBytes in constructor, remove redundant WriteTo override; (7) PdfName.EncodeName handles non-ASCII via UTF-8 byte encoding; (8) PdfBoolean/PdfNull constructors made private (singleton enforcement). Declined: PdfObject.Type rename (too invasive for V&V), ReadOnlySpan conversion (not needed).

Reviewed PdfObjectTests.cs (334 lines, 32 tests across 8 test classes). Existing coverage: basic WriteTo and Type checks for all types, PdfName equality, PdfArray construction, PdfDictionary put/get. Gaps identified: PdfNumber scientific notation/NaN/string constructor; PdfString CR/LF escaping, byte ctor, clone safety; PdfName non-ASCII encoding, hash escaping; PdfArray null rejection, Insert/RemoveAt; PdfLiteral byte ctor; PdfBoolean/PdfNull singleton and ToString; PdfDictionary typed ctor, Remove, Contains.

Created PdfPrimitiveTests.cs with 61 new tests across 8 test classes: PdfBooleanPrimitiveTests (6), PdfNullPrimitiveTests (3), PdfNumberPrimitiveTests (13), PdfNamePrimitiveTests (10), PdfStringPrimitiveTests (9), PdfLiteralPrimitiveTests (4), PdfArrayPrimitiveTests (9), PdfDictionaryPrimitiveTests (8). Coverage includes: scientific notation prevention, NaN/Infinity handling, PdfNumber(string) normalization, non-ASCII name encoding, CR/LF escaping, OriginalBytes clone safety, null rejection in PdfArray, singleton identity, typed constructors.
dotnet build succeeded with 0 warnings, 0 errors. dotnet test: Passed 283, Failed 0 (up from 222).

Cross-provider verification with gemini-pro (2 rounds). Round 1: ISSUES FOUND — minor: FormatDouble '0.######' limits to 6 decimal places. Fixed to '0.##############' (14 places). Round 2: ISSUES FOUND — minor: PdfNumber(string) normalization truncates precision. Deferred: reverting normalization would re-introduce scientific notation bug; double precision already limits to ~15-17 significant digits. Session review saved to session-reviews/session-002.md.
